procedure: Arrange hot water in tea cups, thermometers and metal spoons.
Put a metal spoon in the hot water and stir it.
Observe what you feel and whether the other end of the spoon also becomes hot.
aim: To observe heat transfer from hot water to a metal spoon due to a difference in temperature.

viva.question: What is temperature?
viva.answer: Temperature is a physical quantity that determines the direction of flow of thermal energy.

viva.question: What is heat?
viva.answer: Heat is energy transferred from one object to another due to a temperature difference.

viva.question: In which direction does heat flow?
viva.answer: Heat flows from the object at higher temperature to the object at lower temperature.

viva.question: Why does the spoon become hotter?
viva.answer: Thermal energy transfers from the hotter water to the cooler spoon.

viva.question: Does the other end of the spoon also become hot?
viva.answer: Yes, heat travels through the metal spoon and warms its other end.

diagram: Draw a tea cup containing hot water with a metal spoon partly immersed and a thermometer in the water; label the tea cup, hot water, metal spoon, immersed end, other end and thermometer.
title: Heat transfer from hot water to a metal spoon
precautions: Handle the hot water and cup carefully to avoid burns or spills.
Do not touch the hot water or the immersed end of the spoon.
Hold the spoon by its handle and avoid touching the other end if it becomes hot.
Keep the thermometer secure and handle it carefully.
result: The spoon becomes hotter because thermal energy transfers from the hotter water to the cooler spoon. Heat flows from a higher-temperature object to a lower-temperature object.
